rv.q: It’s a powerful and deeply moving meditation on Black masculinity and Black life in Britain.
A feelgood show that plumbs the depths, then, and a choral cry to be heard that leaves you inspired not browbeaten.
If the writing is grandiloquent and self-pitying in places — there’s room to cut at least 30 minutes from the two-and-a-half-hour running time — the performances are note-perfect.
Ryan Calais Cameron's black blockbuster is one of those overnight successes that was years in the making.
A total triumph, and a game-changer for the West End.
This trailblazing ensemble cast do not just perform the play, they live and breathe it in a way that is rarely seen on stage.
It adds up to a remarkable evening, its themes enlivened and illuminated by laughter and affection.
